newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CBA bond issue 150-200 pct oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: CBA bond issue 150-200 pct oversubscribed.

text.p: The Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) said on Thursday its new April 2000 domestic bond issue was about 150 to 200 percent oversubscribed.

The size of the bond issue, which were priced earlier on Thursday, was increased to A$400 million from an originally planned A$250 million due to demand and represents one of the largest single domestic transactions for some time, Wayne Hoy, Chief Manager Financial Markets at CBA told Reuters.
"The story of this issue once again, is the shortage of securities in the market," Hoy said.
The issue, which matures April 15, 2000, was priced at 22 basis points over the Australian government 2000 bond for a reoffer yield of 6.955 percent.
The bonds carry a coupon of 6-3/4 percent and were issued off CBA's new transferable certificate of deposit (TCD) programme announced last week.
Hoy said demand had mainly been from domestic institutions, although there was also interest from overseas, particularly from Asia.
The syndicate for the deal with CBA as lead manager involved Bankers Trust, Citibank, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and SBC Warburg.
